recipes.name: Crunchy Bok Choy Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 large head bok choy, trimmed and cut into bite-size pieces
2 (3 ounce) packages ramen noodles, broken into pieces

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon canola oil in a small frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook and stir almonds in the hot oil until lightly browned, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer almonds to a large salad bowl.
Toss bok choy, green onions, and ramen noodles with the almonds.
Whisk 1/2 cup canola oil, sugar, balsamic vinaigrette dressing, and soy sauce in a separate bowl until combined.
Pour dressing over vegetables and toss to mix.

raw_recipe.headline: Crunchy Bok Choy Salad
raw_recipe.description: This bok choy salad gets its crunch from ramen noodles and toasted almonds. It is then tossed with a balsamic vinaigrette and soy sauce dressing for a flavorful salad.

review.reviewBody: very good salad.I did add canned chicken to it just to give it some meat,with one tsp.chicken bouillion mmmmmmgood

To save on fat, I toasted the almonds in the oven rather than cooking with oil and used a little less oil for the dressing, as well (with no sacrifice to flavor). Added sliced red bell pepper for color and some leftover shredded grilled chicken breast. I didn’t have any ramen noodles, so I used chow mein noodles instead and would use them again. Served with toasted baguette with a yummy compound butter that I’d mixed up early in the day. The dressing had just the right amount of sweetness and is mellow in taste. This was an absolutely delicious salad which will be made often in this house. Thanks, Cookmaster, thoroughly enjoyed your recipe.

We got some Bok choy in our bountiful basket and this recipe was a great way to use it up. Who knew that raw Bok choy could be so tasty? Made a few changes- added one sweet red pepper, decreased the sugar to 1/3 cup, the oil to 1/4 cup (and used grapeola oil for a light fresh taste). Added about a tsp of toasted sesame oil for flavor. Oh, and we didn't have balsamic vinaigrette- so we just used a really high quality aged balsamic vinegar. Next time, I think I will add a can of oranges.

Delicious!! My husband does not usually eat anything green. He used the left over salad for his lunch. I replaced halved cashews for the sliced almonds. This added to the asian flavor. I reduced the sugar to 1/3 cup and added an additional tablespoon of soy to reduce the sweet taste. (I may try 1/4 cup sugar the next time.) I replaced the balsamic vinaigrette with straight balsamic vinegar and topped off with red pepper flakes.

I love the crunch in this salad! The possibilities are endless. I added chicken, carrots, jalapeños and omitted the sugar. The balsamic gives enough sweetness for me and I love throwing in any veggies I have on hand. Keeper!!

This was so good, I couldn't stop eating it! Per other reviews I reduced the sugar to 1/4 and added a sliced red pepper. Otherwise I followed the directions exactly and we loved it. Definitely a keeper!

This was so quick to make and very tasty. My husband loved it and I shared with co-workers. They have the recipe now. One thing I changed was the amount of sugar, cut it down to 1/4 cup. And instead of ramen noodles I used La Chow crispy noodles for individual servings.

Very light & refreshing. I've never had bok choy before & will make this salad again as is or for a main meal with grilled chicken included for a hot summer day meal. I'm changing this from 4 stars to 5 now that hubby has made several times. I absolutely love this salad. We use chow mein noodles but will try with ramen one of these times.
Followed suggestions of others and used chow mein noodles. Julienne sliced carrots added a splash of color for a nice presentation.
I toasted the almonds and left the oil out of the dressing to make an oil free version

The salad is delightful as an accompaniment to a charcuterie board or an appetizer spread. No need to use oil (especially the large amount called for) to toast the nuts, they have enough natural oil within to toast themselves. Also, I added some julienned carrots.

Made this today (3/11/2022). I find it frustrating when recipes call for a "large," "small," "medium," etc. instead of simply giving measurements in cups, tsps., etc. which are exact. What one person considers large, another may think of as medium. I already had a lot of vidalia (sweet) onion chopped so used that instead of green onion. I did not toast the almonds. Aside from spending about 30 minutes chopping up my "large" head of bok choy, this was a pretty easy recipe to assemble. I did not add the almond/ramen noodle mix to the salad. If most of the salad is going to be eaten that day, it probably is OK to add the almond/ramen mix. Any longer and I suspect the noodles will absorb moisture. So, I sprinkled some of the almond/ramen mix on top of my serving. Since I didn't really deviate from the recipe, I'm surprised at all the reviews being 4 or 5 stars. I thought the taste was OK but nothing great. I also am surprised to see the high calorie count on this. One serving = 452 calories. I won't make this again.
Never tried bok choy prior to this. whole family loved it! reduced sugar to half but did everything else the same
Took to a pot luck dinner. Excellent reviews and several wanted the recipe. Husband really liked it.. Next time I may cut the sugar down a bit and add some bacon.
Didn't have the onions but followed the recipe exactly otherwise. Loved it!
Loved this. Made a small switch to chow mein noodles instead of ramen and am looking to try it with spinach instead of bok choy.
My mother served this and I had to have the recipe. Who knew raw bok choy could taste so delicous? Amazing...
